newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says aims to reduce gearing.
newsitem.headline: BHP says aims to reduce gearing.

text.p: Australia's largest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Monday it aimed to reduce its gearing.
BHP managing director John Prescott said the group was not short of capital but it wanted to retain its long-term A credit rating.
"We intend to reduce our gearing," Prescott said.
He said BHP could not now make an acquisition of the size of last year's US$2.4 billion purchase of the Magma Copper Co without impairing its credit rating or making a share issue.
"We could not make any investment of the magnitude of Magama at this time without impairing our rating or going to the shareholders for additional equity," he told a briefing seminar.
He also said that BHP was moving "more towards a resource company than we have (been)".
This additional focus on resource activities would imply a lower debt to equity ratio.
"We recognise we are facing a more competitive and complex business environment," Prescott told BHP's annual results and prospects seminar.
BHP on Friday revealed it had recorded an abnormal loss before tax of A$1.046 billion and an abnormal loss after tax of A$976 million in the year to May 31, 1997.

It said the abnormal losses included a write-down in some North American copper assets of A$550 million, a writedown in steel assets of A$220 million and a writedown in minerals assets of A$189 million.
The abnormal losses cut BHP's net profit for the year to A$410 million, down 60.8 percent from the 1995/96 result of A$1.O46 billion.
